Evan M.: Hi all, CortexHealth wants to run a week-long Private deployment POC. They asked whether we prefer PrivateLink or peering given they run TLS inspection and must provide a strict allowlist. Need clear ask list to send to their netsec.
Jo K.: TL;DR: PrivateLink reduces routing complexity and limits surface area. But if their TLS inspector needs to see client certs (and preserve original src IP) peering (or TGW) is better.
Nina S.: Important: PrivateLink = interface ENIs in customer's VPC. Those ENI IPs will be the source once traffic reaches our connector (so their IDS will see our ENI IPs). If their IPS expects original on-prem IPs, that won't match.
Rahul D.: Ops: Our connector listens on 8443 for Private deployments by default. We support 443 if they insist. For PrivateLink we'll ask them to allow outbound to the ENI IPs we provide plus allow inbound from those ENIs on 8443. Example SG on our side:
```
Type: TCP
Port: 8443
Source: <customer-privatelink_eni_cidrs>
```
If peering, source will be their VPC CIDR.
Lena T.: Add GovCloud note: if customer is in aws-us-gov partition, endpoint naming and ENI behavior differs; ask their cloud team to confirm partition.
Evan M.: Jo, can you make a short checklist we can send to their netsec? Also they want to know cert options for mTLS.
Jo K.: Yep. Draft checklist below to send: 1) Confirm AWS partition (standard vs gov). 2) Pick connectivity mode: PrivateLink OR VPC peering/TGW. 3) If PrivateLink: share VPC ID + subnets + security team contact. 4) If Peering: share VPC CIDRs + routes + on-prem egress IPs. 5) TLS inspection: yes/no + vendor + where in path (before or after proxy). 6) Desired cert model: customer-managed CA or Redwood-issued cert. 7) Allowlist request: we will provide ENI IPs or EIP list depending on plan.
Nina S.: Cert options: a) NLB TLS termination with client cert verification (we can upload their CA to NLB), b) App-level mTLS (connector validates client certs). Note: TLS inspectors often break end-to-end client cert handshake; if they have a TLS intercept middlebox, app-level mTLS may fail.
Ops Bot: Snapshot for thread 3460012345: ENI_CANDIDATES=["10.2.4.15","10.2.4.48","10.3.8.9"]  NLB_EIPS=["54.210.11.7"] PORTS=["8443","443"]
Rahul D.: If they need source IP preservation for logging or DLP, peering is better since AWS peering preserves src IP. For peering, ensure no CIDR overlap and that route tables have the peering route.
Lena T.: Security snippet to include in email (minimal):
```
Customer side:
- Outbound to interface ENIs (PrivateLink) or to our VPC CIDRs (peering) over TCP/443 or 8443
- Allow DNS to resolve endpoint names (if using PrivateLink with private hosted zone)
Our side:
- Ingress from ENI IPs or customer VPC CIDRs to connector NLB on 8443/TCP
```
Evan M.: Any objections if I propose PrivateLink as default for the POC but call out peering as option if they require DPI/source IP preservation?
Jo K.: No objections. Offer Reserved EIPs in front of NLB for more stable allowlisting as a paid option.
Nina S.: Also ask whether they expect us to perform client cert rotation or if they want to manage certs. Operationally, we can rotate if they give us a CA bundle and rotation window.
Evan M.: Great. I'll send the checklist and Infra snapshot to CortexHealth netsec. Assign owners: Jo = checklist + cert flow doc, Rahul = network runbook snippet, Nina = ops note about TLS inspect. I'll update when they respond. Thanks. :handshake:
